# `get_img_file_info`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read metadata (date, size, kind and FITS header fields) for an image or video file on the device.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (logging branch, both builds); the methods catalog lists UNKNOWN / unknown |
| Side-effect tier | D |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xbd320, getImgFileInfo @0xbc960 (64-bit build) |

Checks that the file exists, then reads file metadata and, depending on the kind, FITS header keys, planet-stack sharpen values, WCS solution (through a helper subprocess), precessed coordinates, or MP4 duration. Only the outer existence check can fail the call: secondary read failures omit members. Synchronous with no timeout. The strict-grade section reads MUTATOR / established because the inaccessible-path branch writes a log entry; the methods catalog lists UNKNOWN. Observer tier D: the deeper FITS, WCS and video library paths are not closed, although a native-only reading would be tier B.

Side effects: Reads files and may spawn a WCS helper subprocess; logs when the path is inaccessible. No request-visible change.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_img_file_info"`. [READ] |
| `params` | string\|array\|object | yes | - | Three spellings of the file name: a bare string, an array whose first element is the string, or an object with name. Missing, null, empty array, missing key or non-string fails with 105. The companion app sends the object form. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | Effective name missing or not a string | `expected string param` |
| 255 | Source file not accessible | `file not exist` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

No result on the error paths. Delegated secondary failures never produce an RPC error.

## Example

Request, object-form - As sent by the app; path invented:

```json
{"id":90,"method":"get_img_file_info","params":{"name":"Example/Stacked_example.fit"}}
```

Request, string-form:

```json
{"id":91,"method":"get_img_file_info","params":"Example/Stacked_example.fit"}
```

Reply, ok-fits - Values invented:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_img_file_info","result":{"date":"2026-01-31 21:04:05","size_k":8192,"type":2,"ra_dec_j2000":[83.8,-5.4],"is_solved":true,"header_date":"2026-01-31","bayer_pat":"GRBG","creator":"example","size":[1080,1920],"stack_num":40,"exp_sec":10.0,"tot_exp_sec":400.0},"code":0,"id":90}
```

Reply, missing:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_img_file_info","error":"file not exist","code":255,"id":92}
```
